newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent settles near high on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent settles near high on technical buying.

text.p: IPE Brent futures extended gains to close up 17 cents on Wednesday on market-on-close (MOC) buying and U.S. product strength, brokers said.
Front month September settled up 17 cents at $18.39 a barrel after last trading at the high of $18.43. October closed up 11 cents at $18.40.
Brent derived late strength from a U.S. gasoline rally based on calendar spread buying by a major Wall Street firm that was said to be acting for commecial players.
Front month NYMEX crude was up 18 cents at $19.66 a barrel. August gasoline was up 1.08 cent at 61.10 cent a gallon. August heating was up 0.62 cent at 53.32 cent a gallon.
Sentiment was also helped by DOE data showing U.S. crude stocks fell 2.0 million barrels last week, compared with a rise of 1.42 million shown in API data late on Tuesday.
In London Brent drew additional strength from firmer physical Brent, which moved at a fresh high backed by a tight prompt market, absent Iraqi barrels and constructive paper positions.
The August 4-6 loading cargo moved to a refiner at August plus 15 cents, five cents higher than a deal on Tuesday and 10 cents above Monday's transaction.
But both crude and gas oil were likely to continue to trade in narrow ranges until there was further news on the resumption of Iraqi crude exports, brokers said.
Reports from U.N. headquarters in New York indicated an aid distribution plan, which Iraq says must be finalised before exports can resume, will not be approved before the weekend.
Traders expected that agreeing new price formulae and signing new contracts will take a further two weeks, suggesting an earliest sales start date of mid-August.
Physical north-west European products were firmer, despite the higher dollar crimping demand. Front month August gas oil settled at $165.00 a tonne, up $2 and 25 cents off the high.
